To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the introduction of E6 in neuroblastoma cells down regulates p53, which leads to morphologic conversion of neuroblastic cells to fibroblast like cells, and that the ability of the cells to form colonies on soft agar is significantly reduced.
the p53 protein in neuroblastoma derived cells is functional, that its inactivation leads to a morphologic conversion of these cells, and that these cells are no longer tumorigenic.

p53 inactivation in SK N SH neuroblastoma cells by the human papillomavirus E6 oncoprotein results in the conversion of the neuroblatic N type cells to the substrate attached S type cells, and that these cells are unable to form colonies in agar, indicating that the p53 inactivated cells have lost tumorigenic potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neuroblastic tumors, which are among the most aggressive of childhood tumors.
the identification of factors that regulate the transdifferentiation process in neuroblastoma derived cells.
the role of p53 in maintaining the malignant phenotype of neuroblastoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53 inactivation in SK N SH neuroblastoma cells results in the loss of the N type morphology and a loss of the ability to form colonies in agar.
the p53 in neuroblastoma cells is functionally intact, but is sequestered in the cytoplasm and is required for maintenance of the tumorigenic phenotype of neuroblastoma cells.
E6 expression in neuroblastoma cells results in a loss of the neuroblasts and a conversion to the fibroblast morphology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

E6 mediated p 53 degradation results in the loss of neuroblastic morphology, loss of neurofilaments and vimentin, loss of retinoic acid responsiveness, loss of anchorage independent growth, and a reduction in tumorigenicity.
E6 mediated p 53 degradation in SK N SH cell line results in the loss of the neuroblastoma phenotype, and the cells become less tumorigenic.
E6 mediated p 53 inactivation resulted in the conversion of SK NSH cells into the substrate adherent phenotype and a reduced capacity to grow in soft agar.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the morphologic conversion of neuroblastoma cells to a substrate adherent phenotype can be induced by inactivating p53, and that the p53 protein in neuroblastoma cells may be a potential therapeutic target.
p53 is a key player in maintaining the tumorigenic phenotype of neuroblastoma cells.
E6 mediated p63 degradation in neuroblastoma cells resulted in a morphologic conversion from neuroblastic cells to a fibroblast like morphology and a reduction in tumorigenic potential.
